cross_check.title: Cross-check with NASA's independent global record

ours.label: Our data (NASA POWER / MERRA-2), whole Earth, area weighted

arctic.label: Our data, Arctic only (north of 60 N)

antarctica.label: Our data, Antarctica only (south of 60 S)

reference.label: NASA GISTEMP v4 (stations and ships, a different method)

cross_check.plain: From 2001 to 2025, NASA's GISTEMP record warms the planet +0.25 °C per decade. Our data gives +0.17 for the whole Earth, because it shows Antarctica cooling (-0.23); without Antarctica it gives +0.20, and the two 95% ranges overlap. Our data also shows the Arctic warming fastest (+0.35 °C per decade), the pattern known as Arctic amplification. The datasets measure slightly different things (air at 2 m vs surface and sea temperature), so we show both numbers instead of hiding the gap.

false_alarms.title: How often the test cries wolf
false_alarms.method: Sen's slope + Mann-Kendall with effective sample size correction (decision D1)
false_alarms.plain: We made 20,000 fake 25-year series with Egypt's real noise and NO trend, and ran our real engine on them. It called 1.0% of them a trend (the target is about 5%). With strong year-to-year resemblance it called 6.8%. The team compared 7 methods on 20,000 series before choosing this one (decision D1).

many_places.title: Testing many places at once
many_places.plain: Egypt has 357 grid cells. Testing each at p < 0.05 would show about 18 'trends' by pure luck even if nothing changed. Without correction 197 cells pass; after the false discovery rate correction 131 remain, and those are the ones the map calls proven.

farming.title: Common-sense checks of the farming outlook

checks.check: Date palms do better in Aswan than in the Delta
Wheat grows in the Delta's winter
Rain alone cannot grow wheat anywhere in Egypt

limitations: Each grid cell is about 55 by 60 km: it describes a region, not one farm.
NASA POWER is a model built from satellites and weather stations (MERRA-2): very good on large scales, less exact for one valley or oasis.
25 years is enough to detect strong trends; small ones may stay 'not proven' until more years are measured.
Future views assume today's measured trend continues in a straight line. They are not forecasts and ignore irrigation changes, new crop varieties and soil.
Crop needs come from FAO ECOCROP averages; real varieties differ, and soil, salinity and water supply are not included.
We never claim why something changes; we say a pattern is consistent with a cause.
